prompt: Where does the code of an Espresso test run while it tests Tickets?
hint: Lesson 14 called it an instrumented test.

choices.text: On your computer, sending commands through adb
choices.why: That is closer to Appium; Espresso is packed into a test APK and runs on the device.

choices.text: In the app's own process, on the device
choices.why: Right. The test APK's instrumentation starts the app, and the two share a process and a main thread.

choices.text: In a second app beside Tickets, talking to it over the screen
choices.why: The test APK is installed beside it, but the tests run inside the app's process, not in one of their own.

choices.text: On the computer's Java runtime, without Android
choices.why: That is a local test, in src/test; Espresso needs a device.

prompt: Tickets starts a thread to fetch the shows. Why does Espresso not wait for it on its own?
hint: What does Espresso watch before every step?

choices.text: Because Espresso never waits for anything
choices.why: It waits for the main thread before every action and check; that is its main feature.

choices.text: Because network calls are forbidden in tests
choices.why: They are forbidden on the main thread, in apps and tests alike; the load is allowed on its own thread.

choices.text: Its thread is not the main one
choices.why: Right. A thread the app started itself is invisible to it.

choices.text: Because the thread runs in boxoffice, not in the app
choices.why: The thread runs in the app's process; boxoffice is the server it asks.

prompt: Which of these can an Espresso test do that an Appium test cannot?
hint: Think of what being inside the process gives.

choices.text: Set Shows.baseUrl before the list loads
choices.why: Right. It shares the app's memory, so the app's own objects are reachable.

choices.text: Choose a list row by the Show object behind it
choices.why: Right. onData reads the adapter's items, which only code inside the app can see.

choices.text: Tap Allow on Android's notification permission dialog
choices.why: The dialog belongs to Android, outside the app's windows; that needs a test from outside (lesson 21).

choices.text: Run the same test against the iOS version of Tickets
choices.why: Espresso is Android only; neither tool runs one test on both without the apps agreeing on names.

prompt: Match each folder of the Tickets project to what lives there.
hint: The table of section 03.

pairs.right: local tests, on the computer's Java runtime
instrumented tests, run on the device

prompt: What does androidTestImplementation(libs.androidx.espresso.core) in the build file mean for the app a user downloads?
hint: Which APK is it for?

choices.text: The app carries Espresso, switched off
choices.why: It is not in the app at all; it goes only into the test APK.

choices.text: Nothing: Espresso goes into the test APK only
choices.why: Right. androidTestImplementation is for the instrumented tests and never reaches a user.

choices.text: The app becomes larger by the size of Espresso
choices.why: That would be implementation; the test configuration keeps the library out of the app.

choices.text: The app can be tested only on an emulator
choices.why: Instrumented tests run on any device adb lists, a phone included.

prompt: Why does the test expect the text R$ 65,00 on the show screen of sh-103?
hint: Look at the capture of the shows, and at price() in Shows.kt.

choices.text: Because that is the price of every show
choices.why: sh-101 and sh-102 cost 8000 cents, so R$ 80,00.

choices.text: Because the app rounds 6500 cents up
choices.why: price() divides whole cents with no rounding: 6500 is exactly 65 reais.

choices.text: Because the layout of the show screen writes it
choices.why: The layout has no text in price; ShowActivity fills it from the intent.

choices.text: boxoffice's 6500 cents, as price() writes them
choices.why: Right. The expected value comes from the API's answer through the app's own formatting.

prompt: Why does the test reach the row of sh-103 with onData instead of onView?
hint: What does a ListView do with its rows when you scroll?

choices.text: A ListView reuses a few row views
choices.why: Right. onData asks the adapter for the item and scrolls to it, so rows off screen are found too.

choices.text: onView cannot find views that have an id
choices.why: onView with withId is the commonest line in Espresso.

choices.text: onData is faster because it skips the main thread
choices.why: Both wait for the main thread; the reason is how a list keeps its rows.

choices.text: Rows in a list carry no id
choices.why: Each row has the ids title and detail, three times over, which is part of the problem.

prompt: On the list screen, before any tap, a test runs onView(withId(R.id.title)).check(matches(isDisplayed())). What happens?
hint: How many views have the id title on that screen?

choices.text: It passes, checking the first row
choices.why: Espresso does not pick one of several; it refuses.

choices.text: It fails with NoMatchingViewException instead
choices.why: That is for no match at all; here there are three.

choices.text: It fails with AmbiguousViewMatcherException
choices.why: Right. Every row has a title, so the matcher finds three views where it must find one.

choices.text: It checks the show screen's title instead
choices.why: The show screen is not open; nothing was tapped.

prompt: The banner of Tickets is hidden with visibility gone. Which check passes on a fresh list?
hint: Is the view there or not?

choices.text: check(doesNotExist())
choices.why: The view exists in the layout on every start, so this fails.

choices.text: check(matches(not(isDisplayed())))
choices.why: Right. It exists and is not displayed.

choices.text: check(matches(isDisplayed()))
choices.why: It is hidden until the app is offline with a saved copy.

choices.text: check(matches(withText("")))
choices.why: A text check says nothing about whether it is shown, which is the question.

prompt: In onData(showWithId("sh-103")).inAdapterView(withId(R.id.shows)).perform(click()), the custom matcher extends Espresso's ___, which only looks at items of one class.
hint: Bounded to Show.

prompt: In the grep of MainActivity.kt, on which line is Shows.busy lowered?
hint: The line with busy--.

prompt: Why does MainActivity lower busy inside runOnUiThread, after display, and not at the end of the background thread?
hint: When is the screen finished?

choices.text: Because a background thread cannot change a number
choices.why: Any thread can; busy is even marked volatile for that.

choices.text: So busy reaches zero only once the list is on screen
choices.why: Right. Lowered earlier, Espresso would go on between the answer arriving and the list being drawn.

choices.text: Because Espresso reads busy only on the background thread
choices.why: The idling resource reads it on the main thread; the order matters, not the reader.

choices.text: So that a failed load does not lower it
choices.why: Every load lowers it, failed or not; display handles all three results.

prompt: A colleague fixes the flaky ListTest with Thread.sleep(3000) before onData. It has passed fifty times. What do you tell them?
hint: What does the test wait for, and for how long?

choices.text: Fine, but 5000 would be safer on CI
choices.why: A longer guess is still a guess, and costs more on every run.

choices.text: Fine: fifty passes prove the race is gone
choices.why: The race is still there; the sleep only makes losing it rarer, until a load takes longer than three seconds.

choices.text: Use an idling resource on Shows.busy
choices.why: Right. It waits exactly as long as the load, fails with a name, and says what the test waits for.

choices.text: Move the sleep into the app's MainActivity
choices.why: That slows down every user to fix a test.

prompt: Why does ShowsIdlingResource post a new check every tenth of a second while busy is above zero?
hint: Who tells the resource that busy dropped?

choices.text: Because Espresso requires every resource to poll
choices.why: A resource the app notifies, like CountingIdlingResource, never polls.

choices.text: The app never says when busy drops
choices.why: Right. It asks again itself, and calls Espresso back the first time the answer is zero.

choices.text: To make the load itself finish sooner
choices.why: The checks only read busy; they cannot speed up a request to boxoffice.

choices.text: Because isIdleNow may only run on the load thread
choices.why: The checks are posted to the main thread, on purpose.

prompt: The offline test points Shows.baseUrl at http://10.0.2.2:9 rather than at an address nobody answers, like 10.255.255.1. Why?
hint: Compare the two curl captures.

choices.text: Because 10.255.255.1 would reach the emulator itself
choices.why: Only localhost is the emulator itself; 10.255.255.1 goes out to a network where nothing answers it.

choices.text: A refused port fails at once, the other waits 5 s
choices.why: Right. curl was refused after 0 ms and gave up after 5002 ms, and the app has the same 5000 ms limit.

choices.text: Because port 9 makes boxoffice return an error
choices.why: boxoffice listens on 8080; nothing at all answers on port 9.

choices.text: Because the emulator cannot reach private addresses
choices.why: 10.0.2.2 is itself a private address the emulator reaches.

prompt: A test clears the saved copy, sets Shows.baseUrl to the dead address and forgets to restore it. ListTest runs after it in the same run. What happens, and why?
hint: How long does a Kotlin object live during an instrumented run?

choices.text: It fails: Shows outlives each test in one process
choices.why: Right. The tests share a process, so the changed address leaks into every later test, depending on order.

choices.text: Nothing: each test class gets a fresh copy of the app
choices.why: The activity is fresh; the process and its objects are not.

choices.text: ListTest passes, using a copy saved earlier
choices.why: The forgetful test cleared the copy, so there is none to fall back on.

choices.text: The rule of ListTest resets baseUrl before each test
choices.why: ActivityScenarioRule opens an activity; it knows nothing of Shows.

prompt: Why does OfflineTest open the activity with ActivityScenario.launch rather than with the rule ListTest uses?
hint: When does the first load read baseUrl?

choices.text: Because the rule cannot open MainActivity
choices.why: It opens it in ListTest; the problem is when.

choices.text: Because launch skips the first load
choices.why: launch opens the activity normally, and onCreate starts the load as always.

choices.text: baseUrl must change before onCreate's first load
choices.why: Right. The rule opens the activity before the test body runs, too early to change anything.

choices.text: Because launch clears SharedPreferences on its own
choices.why: The @Before does that, with clear().commit().

prompt: Which Gradle task runs the instrumented tests on every device adb lists?
hint: Connected, and the debug variant.

choices.text: ./gradlew test
choices.why: That runs the local tests in src/test, on the computer.

choices.text: ./gradlew assembleDebug
choices.why: That builds the app's APK and runs nothing.

choices.text: ./gradlew connectedDebugAndroidTest
choices.why: Right. It builds both APKs, installs them and runs the tests.

choices.text: ./gradlew installDebug
choices.why: That installs the app only; no test runs.

prompt: Why does the lesson switch off the three animation scales on the emulator before running Espresso?
hint: What does Espresso wait for, and how does an animation run?

choices.text: Espresso does not reliably wait them out
choices.why: Right. It is Google's advice for every device that runs Espresso.

choices.text: To make the emulator use less memory
choices.why: The reason is synchronisation, not memory.

choices.text: Because Tickets's animations hide the defects
choices.why: Tickets has no animations of its own; the system's transitions are the issue.

choices.text: Because adb refuses to install with animations on
choices.why: Installation does not care about animations.

prompt: Put the steps of noServerWithACopyShowsTheBanner in the order the test runs them.
hint: A copy has to be saved before boxoffice disappears.
items: clear the saved copy and register the idling resource
launch MainActivity, whose first load reaches boxoffice
check the list, so Espresso waits for that load
point Shows.baseUrl at the dead address and tap refresh
check the banner and its words
put the address back and unregister

prompt: In OfflineTest's second test, the line onView(withId(R.id.shows)).check(matches(isDisplayed())) is deleted. Sometimes the banner check now fails. Why?
hint: What did that check make Espresso wait for?

choices.text: The list is no longer displayed without that check
choices.why: A check observes; it does not make the list appear.

choices.text: The idling resource stops working without an onView first
choices.why: It works for any onView or onData; the problem is what happens before the next one.

choices.text: The banner shows the wrong time
choices.why: The check stops before the time, so the time cannot fail it.

choices.text: No copy is saved before the address changes
choices.why: Right. That check was the sync point; without it the address changes while the first load is out, that load fails too, and with no copy the app shows the error line.

prompt: Match each need of a Tickets test to the tool of lessons 15 and 16 that meets it.
hint: Inside the process or outside it?

pairs.left: make boxoffice unreachable by changing Shows.baseUrl
tap Allow on Android's permission dialog
wait for a load on the app's own thread
wait for a row to appear on the screen, from outside
pairs.right: an explicit wait such as waitForDisplayed
